summary: Journeys against a running Workshop, from another Loom host's session: inspect it, drive it, picture it.

tools.name: connections
tools.summary: Ask Workshop's guest door who is connected, and find this session's own row.
tools.description: Asks the link which far session it holds and under which name Workshop admitted it, then asks Workshop's guest door (zengine.guests) for its connection inventory and checks that the row for that far session is admitted under that name. Writes the inventory as JSON. Changes nothing in Workshop.

inputs.name: link
inputs.help: the external host's link to the Workshop (its asks below name link 'workshop')

outputs.name: connections.json
outputs.help: the guest door's inventory, as answered

requires: a running Workshop started with a guests file whose row for this host may 'inspect'
a link named 'workshop' in the session's boot plan, admitted by that Workshop
zengine-guest-vocabulary booted in the session host (Workshop's shapes, declared there)
tools.recovery: 'unlinked' means the link has no far session (the Workshop is not running or refused this host: see loom-session status). A dispatch refusal from Workshop means its guests file does not let this host 'inspect'.

tools.name: inspect-capture
tools.summary: Inspect a running Workshop, take its picture, press a key chord through an input session, and take the picture again.
tools.description: The journey, in order, each step checked against its owner's answer: the link's own session; this session's row in the guest door's inventory; an input session from zengine.input; a picture of what Workshop presents, fetched chunk by chunk and checked whole; optionally a picture ARMED for the next painted frame, so a capture waits at Workshop's Skin; optionally a hold at a release gate; the chord injected with settlement, so the answer comes back only once Workshop has dispatched everything the injection set in motion; the armed picture, if any; the picture after the chord; the session closed. Every failure after the session opened closes it first, and says both.

inputs.name: link
inputs.help: the external host's link to the Workshop

inputs.name: chord
inputs.help: the key chord to press, e.g. ctrl+p, down, escape, ctrl+shift+f

inputs.name: text
inputs.help: text to type after the chord

inputs.name: arm
inputs.help: ask for the picture of the next painted frame BEFORE pressing the chord, so a real capture is pending at Workshop's Skin until the chord's repaint answers it

inputs.name: hold
inputs.help: hold before the chord until <run>/release/<hold> exists; empty: never

inputs.name: await_repaint
inputs.help: with arm: wait for Workshop to paint by itself before pressing the chord -- for a Workshop that changes on its own

inputs.name: await_seconds
inputs.help: how long await_repaint waits: this tool's own decision to stop waiting, never a verdict about Workshop

inputs.name: changed
inputs.help: require the picture after the chord to differ from the one before it

inputs.name: bug_after
inputs.help: raise an error on purpose after this step (inspect, open, inject) -- a tool bug, for seeing failure and cleanup

outputs.name: connections.json
outputs.help: the guest door's inventory, as answered

outputs.name: before.<bmp|cells.txt>
outputs.help: what Workshop presented once the input session was open

outputs.name: armed.<bmp|cells.txt>
outputs.help: with arm: the picture that waited at the Skin for the next painted frame

outputs.name: after.<bmp|cells.txt>
outputs.help: what it presented after everything the chord set in motion was dispatched

requires: a running Workshop started with a guests file whose row for this host may 'input', 'capture' and 'inspect'
a link named 'workshop' in the session's boot plan, admitted by that Workshop
zengine-guest-vocabulary booted in the session host
the input session free: Workshop admits one holder at a time, and every run on one link is the same holder to it
tools.recovery: An input session refused as 'busy' means another holder has it -- on the same link, that is another run of this session, because Workshop sees every run on one link as one participant: wait for it, or use a second link. 'lost' means the link went down after a request was submitted: its outcome is UNKNOWN and nothing is resent; Workshop's guest door closes a lost guest's input session itself. A picture refused 'one waits at a time' means another capture is armed at the Skin.
